A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSW-SL research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original gradient-flow, GAN, diffusion-model, and color-transfer experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E, including numerical results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the splitting-map Radon transform, TSW-SL/MaxTSW-SL definitions, and generative-model objectives are retained. New Appendix B.3 illustrates the existing computation; the equivariance remark does not introduce an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Swiss Roll, 25 Gaussians, high-dimensional Gaussians, color transfer, GANs on CIFAR-10/CelebA/STL-10, and CIFAR-10 diffusion models. Spherical and graph settings mentioned in the new discussion add no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: SW, MaxSW, SWGG, and LCVSW in Table 1; SW and Orthogonal-SW in Table 5; DDGAN and SW-DD in Table 4; and the same color-transfer comparators in v2 Figure 6/v3 Figure 10.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same sample counts, projection counts, preprocessing, learning rates, metrics, and training budgets, including 2500 gradient-flow iterations and 1800 diffusion epochs. No new experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The line-count ablation in Table 5, qualitative generation examples, and diffusion training-curve analysis are unchanged. New Figures 5–8 explain projections and subtree construction through a worked example, rather than reporting a new ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 still report averages over 10 runs, while Tables 3 and 6 retain three-run averages with the same ± reporting. No seed information, uncertainty procedure, or significance testing is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their entries and values; for example, Table 4 reports FIDs of 3.64, 2.90, and 2.83 for DDGAN, SW-DD, and TSW-SL-DD in both versions. Color-transfer results, generated samples, and diffusion curves also match after renumbering.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, and proofs in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–D are retained. B.3 applies the existing subtree-mass formula to an illustrative example, and Appendix F discusses cited extensions without introducing new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same geometric construction, injectivity, metricity, efficiency, and empirical-advantage claims. The qualification that the primary comparison is against original SW also remains.

C2.justification: A new B.1 remark suggests equivariance conditions could improve splitting maps. New Appendix F discusses applicability to dynamic-support measures, possible limitations of bounded partition/clustering trees, and Sobolev transport for higher-order or graph settings.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the architectures, hyperparameters, training instructions, A100 hardware, runtimes, and code-source attributions. B.3 provides explanatory calculations without adding implementation settings or changing code/data access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning relative to distance-based, nonlinear-projection, and spherical tree-sliced extensions, partition/clustering tree metrics, and Sobolev transport. It also expands application/equivariance citations and removes Takezawa et al. (2022), while retaining the main contribution positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds explanatory subsection B.3, Further Discussions, an equivariance remark, and acknowledgements. It removes the appendix table of contents and moves Broader Impact from F to G. Remaining edits are localized wording, capitalization, affiliation, and conference-header changes.

P2.justification: New Figures 5–8 provide a coordinated walkthrough of projection, mass assignment, and induced trees. Existing appendix Figures 5–8 become 9–12. Figure sizing, placement, and the Figure 3 caption receive limited adjustments; empirical displays and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.3 makes the existing transport computation easier to follow through diagrams and explicit subtree-mass calculations, while Appendix F adds useful context about scope and related approaches. These are limited explanatory gains with unchanged scientific evidence. Removing the appendix contents list slightly weakens navigation but does not outweigh those gains.
